name: Prof. Colleen Loo
title: Professor of Psychiatry
bio:
Colleen Loo is a clinical psychiatrist and Professor of Psychiatry at UNSW Sydney and the Black Dog Institute, Randwick. She is an internationally recognised expert in electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) and ketamine for depression.

She led the first Australian randomised controlled trials of TMS and ketamine in depression and established novel treatment clinics at the Black Dog Institute and Ramsay Clinic Northside. Her work spans clinical trials, neuroimaging, and real-world treatment data through the CARE network.

Prof. Loo has published over 300 peer-reviewed papers and advises Australian government health departments and the Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists on neurostimulation policy.

name: Scientia Prof. Gordon Parker
title: Scientia Professor of Psychiatry
bio:
Scientia Professor Gordon Parker is a Scientia Professor of Psychiatry at UNSW Sydney and founder of the Black Dog Institute. Over five decades he has led clinical and research programs in mood disorders, served as Head of the UNSW School of Psychiatry, and received the 2020 Australian Mental Health Prize.

His research focuses on depression classification, bipolar disorder, and translating psychiatric research into clinical practice across the Randwick Health & Innovation Precinct.

name: Prof. Samuel Harvey

bio:
Professor Samuel Harvey is Executive Director and Chief Scientist at the Black Dog Institute and Professor of Psychiatry at UNSW Sydney. His research addresses workplace mental health, depression prevention, and the epidemiology of mental disorders.

He leads large-scale cohort studies and intervention trials that inform policy across Australia and internationally, with strong links to SESLHD clinical services at Randwick.

Her research translates evidence-based digital tools into clinical and community settings across the RHIP precinct.
